items.title: Howard Mandel interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 9, 2003
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] ...I heard this anecdote about a critic who had written about Albert Ayler... [INTERVIEWEE] I’ve had that circumstance but I don’t necessarily try to reign it in...

ctx.x: And I think that his perspective on what he does — I do not think that musicians share the perspective that jazz critics share on the music. Musicians are focused on what they’re doing and they understand what they’re doing internally. They’re not necessarily able to articulate it, and we’re not looking to them to do that. I think a good jazz journalist who is doing interviews helps the musician to articulate what they’re doing for the reader. But we can help them because we’re supposed to be good with words the…

Do you find it difficult sometimes to let’s say reign in your own opinions about whether songs, particular songs from artists have a meaning beyond the music? And what I mean © Fillius Jazz Archive -15-

by that, I heard this anecdote about a critic who had written about Albert Ayler and was imposing his own feelings about the music that Albert was playing about oppression and his passion and the whole thing, and that Albert read that and said, “That’s not what I was thinking at all, I was just playing.” So to shorten the question, do you ever have a circumstance where you have to say to yourself maybe this isn’t what this person was about at all?
